name: ALN-6222
lead: ALN-6222 is an investigational RNA interference (RNAi) therapy that targets INHBE, a gene linked to fat distribution, in people with obesity. It is not approved for any use.[1]

Its only public footprint in the sources reviewed is a Phase 1 trial registration (NCT07624071), which started on 4 June 2026, is recruiting, and plans to enroll 88 participants.[1] No results have been reported.

paras: One Phase 1 trial in participants with obesity (88 planned) is registered and recruiting, having started on 4 June 2026.[1] No results have been identified.

refs.title: A Study to Evaluate ALN-6222 in Participants With Obesity (NCT07624071)

card.summary: An experimental INHBE-targeting RNAi drug that has just entered its first obesity trial; nothing is known about results.
card.note: Investigational only; no published human data.

quick.overview:
ALN-6222 is an experimental RNA interference drug aimed at the INHBE gene and is in an early Phase 1 trial for obesity.

No results exist yet.
quick.mechanism: RNAi drugs lower production of a chosen protein by silencing its gene; the target here is INHBE.
quick.risks: No safety data have been reported. The drug is investigational and not available by prescription.
